items.title: Howard Mandel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003

ctx.x: And so that gave me a sense that there was a way of arriving at something in a different structure, I mean that’s okay? All right. I can buy that then. And I think this was one of my intellectual snobbery, and rock & roll and pop music just didn’t seem, I don’t know, sophisticated enough or interesting, and the singing, especially twelve, thirteen, when I was twelve and thirteen was when the Beatles came on the scene. And they were singing yeah-yeah-yeah and I was like no-no-no. You know, this is just too dumb.…
You must have been an avid reader.
